Start with the industry mechanism

Who benefits. Who loses. Why.

Wealth buys access, time and scarce services. Financial pressure changes what households can afford, share, repair or give up. Explore both sides, one transmission chain at a time.

The premise needs a qualification: uneven spending power is better supported than “everyone below the rich is getting poorer.” Income, liquid wealth, housing tenure and essential bills create different constraints.
Evidence, time periods and limits

Ranked diligence priorities Operating evidence, valuation gates and break conditions

Qualitative research priorities, not a forecast of returns. The ranking favors a measurable bottleneck, documented revenue and a falsifiable test. Entry valuation can reverse the ordering.

01. Serviced sites and completed housing placements

The bottleneck is a permitted, connected and financeable home. Underwriting the completed installation makes the demand-to-cash bridge more concrete than buying national factory capacity alone.

Exposures: UMH (NYSE); CVCO (NASDAQ); SKY (NYSE)

Valuation gate: Use project returns after all connection and carrying costs. No national utility or pipe manufacturer is designated a pure play. Compare recurring cash earnings per share with fully funded infill cost; gross property growth is insufficient if financing dilutes common holders. Dated 2–3 October 2026 observation and illustrative scenario, not a price target: $15.41 last-trade snapshot implies 15.26x $1.01 guided normalized FFO. Illustrative $0.10–$0.30/share reserves reduce cash-proxy yield to 5.91–4.61%. Validate actual reserves and refinancing before treating FFO as distributable cash.

Monitor: Serviced sites delivered; Connection fees and schedules; Cost per occupied site; Occupied versus developed sites; Cash collections

Break condition: Permitted sites fail to become occupied homes at a cost consistent with affordable rents. Occupancy or collections deteriorate despite available sites, or rent limits prevent acceptable investment returns.

Themes: Housing expansion needs roads, water and connections Scarce permitted homesites capture recurring rent Factory-built homes win on the complete delivered bill

02. Financial administration for complex wealth

Multi-entity ownership needs reconciliation, custody and fiduciary work even when transactions slow. Separate fee growth from asset-price appreciation and staff expense.

Exposures: NTRS (NASDAQ); SCHW (NYSE)

Valuation gate: Assess incremental service margin and client concentration; assets administered are not equivalent to revenue-producing AUM. Value recurring administration after staffing and fiduciary costs; do not price a general estate-tax emergency that current federal rules do not support.

Monitor: GFO fees and margin; Organic family relationships; Outsourcing penetration and service staffing; Trust/estate mandates; Organic servicing fees

Break condition: The outsourcing thesis weakens if families increasingly internalize services or fees per unit of operational complexity decline materially. The margin thesis weakens if administrative complexity is absorbed within existing fees or automation and competition reduce billable work faster than mandates grow.

Themes: Very large fortunes create demand for a financial operating system Complex ownership supports legal and fiduciary coordination Independent advice still needs custody and administration

03. Necessary vehicle maintenance and parts availability

A work-critical vehicle creates a concrete willingness to repair, but the exhaustion-of-cash branch is an explicit opposing exposure. Availability and inventory returns matter more than fleet age alone.

Exposures: ORLY (NASDAQ); DORM (NASDAQ); LKQ (NASDAQ)

Valuation gate: Separate price growth and repurchases from unit economics. A strong operating business can deliver poor returns from an excessive entry multiple. Dated 2–3 October 2026 observation and illustrative scenario, not a price target: $84.90 snapshot / $3.25 guided EPS = 26.12x. A 10% five-year price-return hurdle at 20x terminal earnings requires 16.0% EPS CAGR (dividends excluded). Verify a credible earnings bridge or demand a lower entry price. Value regional cash earnings and debt separately; an unresolved strategic review is not a guaranteed premium.

Monitor: Repair orders and unit volumes; Vehicle age and scrappage; DIY versus professional mix; Alternative-parts utilization; Repairable claims

Break condition: Repair transactions fall persistently despite fleet aging and parts availability. Alternative share stalls or rising sourcing costs eliminate the repair-cost advantage.

Themes: Keeping cars longer supports necessary maintenance Repair budgets shift toward recycled and aftermarket components Severe cash shortages can overwhelm the repair trade

04. Private-aviation maintenance and usable airport capacity

The installed fleet creates work after the initial purchase. Technician supply, certification and airport access can constrain capacity; contract economics and conglomerate dilution determine capture.

Exposures: BBD.B (TSX); FlightSafety is owned by Berkshire; specialist training capacity and private providers are the more exact economic exposure.; Private terminal operators such as Signature; airport ground leases and hangar property, subject to local rights and restrictions.

Valuation gate: Value repeat service contribution after technicians, parts inventory and incremental hangar capacity, distinguishing recurring maintenance from discretionary refurbishment. A price implying service margins rise automatically with fleet size is demanding if staffing and turnaround constraints require substantial reinvestment or pricing fails to cover labor. Underwrite simulator utilization, recurrent contracts and instructor costs against full equipment replacement and accreditation capital. A price assuming permanently full training slots must survive added capacity and changing aircraft types; the economic channel is too small to justify a broad parent-company premium by itself.

Monitor: Service revenue and cash margin; Aircraft downtime and repair turnaround; Technician vacancies versus capacity; Training-slot availability; Simulator utilization and capital returns

Break condition: Fleet growth does not translate into sustained service work, or labor/parts costs consume all incremental revenue. Private-fleet expansion occurs without rising training utilization or pricing because existing capacity is ample.

Themes: A larger private fleet creates maintenance demand after the original sale Private fleet growth pulls through recurrent specialist training Private mobility raises the value of usable airport access

05. Collateral liquidity with normalized collateral economics

Pawn provides a defined liquidity service. Distinguish fees and transaction growth from gold prices, acquired operations, inventory realization and non-pawn credit losses.

Exposures: FCFS (NASDAQ)

Valuation gate: Compare normalized earnings and capital tied up in receivables/inventory; stress lower jewelry realizations before paying for peak growth. Dated 2–3 October 2026 observation and illustrative scenario, not a price target: Oct 2 close $210.36 is about 20.7x adjusted earnings proxy and 3.34% adjusted FCF yield. Illustrative legacy-scrap normalization gives $9.48 EPS and about $171 at an assumed 18x; this is a gate, not a target.

Monitor: Same-store loan count versus average principal; Redemption and forfeiture mix; Age of inventory and realized retail margin; Cash return after financing

Break condition: Reject the earnings thesis if receivables grow while fee yield, merchandise turns and cash return on assets deteriorate after collateral-price normalization.

Themes: Pawn converts possessions into short-term liquidity

06. Private-pay aging care with staffing discipline

Households buy dependable care hours and coordination rather than an abstract longevity promise. Occupancy, payer capacity and labor retention offer measurable tests.

Exposures: WELL (NYSE); Private local care agencies: More direct affluent cash-pay exposure than companies dominated by public reimbursement. Risk: Quality, key caregivers, liability and wage-rate spread.; Stabilized senior-living properties: Scarcity can support cash flow and exit value. Risk: Care costs and capitalization-rate changes may outweigh rent growth.

Valuation gate: Do not use publicly reimbursed provider revenue as affluent private-pay exposure. Value sustainable collected contribution per served hour and local referral retention; no aggregate TAM inferred from aging counts. No public pure play verified. Model paid ongoing cases separately from one-time assessments and placement commissions; avoid counting every care recipient as a subscriber.

Monitor: Served versus requested hours; Caregiver retention and wage/billing-rate spread; Geographic scheduling density; Client continuity and adverse events; Paid renewals and referral sources

Break condition: Reject if demand grows but unfilled shifts, turnover and overtime prevent contribution growth, or if clients reduce hours despite greater aggregate wealth. Reject if families do not renew after a crisis, coordination time is merely shifted to the client, or commissions undermine trust.

Themes: Private-pay care converts wealth into hours of independence Care coordination becomes a purchased household function Affluent senior communities bundle housing, care and hospitality

07. Secondhand throughput and useful-item yield

Buyer affordability and seller liquidity are different sides of the same channel. Sorting productivity, usable yield and contribution per order can matter more than gross merchandise volume.

Exposures: SVV (NYSE); TDUP (NASDAQ)

Valuation gate: Compare cash earnings after new-store and warehouse capital; consignment gross margin is not directly comparable with owned-inventory retail gross margin. Model supply conversion and processing contribution rather than valuing gross listed inventory as sales. Private authentication vendors need contracted transaction evidence.

Monitor: Items sold and ticket separately; Gross profit per processed item; Repeat purchase and sell-through; Cash return on new stores; Accepted supply quality

Break condition: Reject if customer growth requires persistent subsidies or higher throughput fails to improve contribution after processing and logistics. Reject the platform thesis if more seller intake raises unsold inventory and costs faster than net marketplace contribution.

Themes: Secondhand can preserve function at a smaller cash ticket Selling possessions supplies cash and resale inventory

08. Employee equity conversion into durable advised assets

Workplace relationships create a route from stock awards to managed financial assets. Conversion, retained fee-bearing assets and servicing costs distinguish the opportunity from headline net new assets.

Exposures: MS (NYSE)

Valuation gate: Do not capitalize an exceptional IPO inflow as recurring annual revenue. Track realized fees and retention before assigning a distribution premium. Dated 2–3 October 2026 observation and illustrative scenario, not a price target: Dated $190.31 snapshot is 15.37x reconstructed $12.38 trailing GAAP EPS, but 18.64x prior-year $10.21 working base. At an assumed 16x exit, a 10% three-year price-return hurdle needs 15.7% EPS CAGR from that base, excluding dividends. Test recurring fee conversion separately from market-cycle profits.

Monitor: Workplace-originated asset inflows; Fee-based conversion after liquidity events; IPO calendar and restrictions

Break condition: The commercial thesis fails if workplace assets leave after selling or remain largely in low-revenue custody rather than paid relationships.

Themes: Employee stock and IPOs create a workplace-to-wealth channel

09. Property operations and scarce service labor

An installed property stock needs recurring maintenance and administration. Labor captures part of the premium, so organic growth and cash returns must be separated from acquisitions and adjusted earnings.

Exposures: FSV (NASDAQ); LTH (NYSE); BBD.B (TSX); Amenity-rich residential property: Useful services may sustain appeal. Risk: Fees, special assessments and obsolescence can offset any resale premium.

Valuation gate: Separate organic service cash flow from acquired growth and normalize restoration; a recurring contract is valuable only after servicing costs and retention. Additional channel evidence: Value the manager's fee/contribution, not total association expenditure or property value. Split Residential from Brands and organic growth from acquisitions. Dated 2–3 October 2026 observation and illustrative scenario, not a price target: Dated $129.13 snapshot is about 36.58x stitched trailing GAAP EPS versus 22.23x adjusted EPS. Include recurring SBC, acquisition amortization, minorities and financing. Q2 Residential organic growth +5% versus Brands -3% argues for segment cash models, not a blanket defensive-services multiple. Use normalized replacement compensation and a realistic support ratio. EBITDA that depends on underpaying scarce professionals or founder overwork is not a durable earnings base. Additional channel evidence: Stress cash margins when wages, vacancies and capacity spending rise faster than realized prices, including delays before new staff become productive. A price assuming full pass-through and unchanged margins embeds successful hiring and productivity; this negative feedback is already reflected only if normalized earnings allow for those costs. Additional channel evidence: No broad listed proxy assigned; assess local customer mix, capacity and incremental margins before valuing a private service business.

Monitor: Organic revenue and contract retention; Margins after labor costs; Assessments, delinquencies and maintenance backlogs; Organic contracts and retention; Fees versus staffing cost

Break condition: The wealth-linked thesis weakens if prosperous communities internalize work or service growth is explained almost entirely by storms and acquisitions. Additional channel evidence: Reject if amenities fail to support renewal or occupancy and households consistently vote to remove them, or manager margins require unsustainable service cuts. The scarcity thesis weakens where supply expands without quality loss and labor cost per service falls despite demand growth; a rollup thesis fails if acquired relationships leave. Additional channel evidence: Service demand grows while availability improves and unit labor costs remain flat, eliminating the predicted bottleneck. Additional channel evidence: The local-demand thesis weakens if wealthy spending shifts abroad or online, or service payroll fails to respond in the relevant labor market.

Themes: Property owners buy recurring operations, amenities and maintenance Scarce labor can capture the premium before shareholders do

10. Private-market liquidity infrastructure

Demand to sell illiquid assets can generate transaction and administration business. Attractive service revenue does not establish an attractive purchase price for the underlying asset.

Exposures: STEP (NASDAQ); BX (NYSE); Secondary private-fund interests: Return depends on entry discount, underlying realizations and financing, not simply the size of the secondary market.; Nontraded evergreen private-credit or private-markets funds: Liquidity depends on contract and board action; stated NAV is not a guaranteed immediate sale price.

Valuation gate: Separate recurring fee economics from unrealized carry; for fund purchases, underwrite cash flows and asset values rather than treating any NAV discount as cheap. Assess underlying net return after all share-class fees and a realistic liquidity discount; manager stocks require separate earnings analysis.

Monitor: Secondary pricing and completed volume; Capital raised versus deployed; Realized distributions and leverage; Requests versus completed repurchases; Net subscriptions after redemptions

Break condition: The earnings thesis fails if growing transaction volume requires lower fees or deteriorating underwriting that causes investors to stop committing. The adverse-liquidity thesis weakens if requests normalize, cash is generated from assets and subscriptions recover without sacrificing underwriting or terms.

Themes: Illiquidity creates a market for secondaries and structured finance Evergreen funds trade easier access for constrained exit

11. DIY beauty with a consolidated cash-flow test

Replacing paid labor with household time is more directly testable than an emotional lipstick-effect story. Retail gains can coexist with weak professional-channel economics.

Exposures: SBH (NYSE); ELF (NYSE)

Valuation gate: Use segment earnings and gross profit per retained routine. A low share price or high apparent gross margin does not establish a cheap stock. Dated 2–3 October 2026 observation and illustrative scenario, not a price target: Oct 2 close $16.24 is 7.9x $2.06 guided EPS. Guided $200m FCF is 12.6% of a diluted-share equity proxy; a 12% no-growth hurdle needs about $191m durable annual FCF. One margin point costs roughly $0.28 EPS under stated assumptions. Normalize tariff refunds and acquisitions before comparing earnings; current price-implied growth is not verified. Brand growth and an attractive security price are separate tests.

Monitor: Professional visit frequency versus at-home replenishment; Units and repeat rates by channel; All-in task time; Segment contribution margins; Organic units and repeat purchase

Break condition: Reject if consumer supplies fail to gain repeat use as service visits fall, or if supply growth is driven only by promotions and new distribution. Reject the trade-down explanation without cohort or basket-switching evidence, and reject the stock thesis if organic contribution fails despite retail share growth.

Themes: Household labor can replace purchased services, within limits Beauty routines may migrate toward value without a universal lipstick effect

12. Premium travel distribution and fee economics

Affluent spending reaches intermediaries and suppliers through different contracts and investment cycles. Fee realization and recurring installed systems deserve separate diligence from hotel asset ownership.

Exposures: MAR (NASDAQ); AC (PARIS); BKNG (NASDAQ); TRIP (NASDAQ); SAF (PARIS)

Valuation gate: Separate recurring owner-paid fees from card-contract changes, acquisitions and room additions; test owner profitability, retention and conversion economics. A price assuming perpetual fee growth needs an economically healthy property base and sustained net openings, rather than simply higher reported brand revenue. Underwrite commissions after paid traffic, refunds, service costs and supplier incentives; verify repeat direct customers reduce acquisition expense. A price requiring stable take rates plus cheaper customer acquisition is demanding if hotels, advisors or AI distribution can bypass the platform; segment declines must remain in the valuation.

Monitor: Comparable room rates and occupancy by chain scale; Net room additions; Fee growth excluding card and acquisition changes; Direct repeat booking mix; Experience bookings net of marketing

Break condition: Luxury fee growth disappears after controlling for room additions, acquisitions and non-room contracts. Customers increasingly coordinate complex trips through direct channels without paying intermediary fees.

Themes: Hotel brands collect fees from affluent travel with limited property capital Complex travel shifts value toward planning and booking intermediaries Airline premiumization creates a separate equipment cycle

13. Tax customization and intergenerational adviser retention

Ownership transfers and tax complexity create service work, while heirs can change advisers. Retention and incremental fee realization need to exceed specialist labor and technology costs.

Exposures: BLK (NYSE); SCHW (NYSE); NTRS (NASDAQ); UBS (NYSE); Owner-occupied housing: Transfers enable entry but can be capitalized into prices; ownership has ongoing cash costs.; Family-funded private business equity: Patient capital can fund productive entry, but nepotism and failed projects also destroy capital.

Valuation gate: Do not capitalize marketed tax alpha as guaranteed fund return. Evaluate the manager on retained fee revenue and platform costs. Use retention-adjusted revenue and normalized costs; a multidecade global transfer estimate is neither annual addressable revenue nor guaranteed organic growth.

Monitor: Net SMA flows and fee rate; After-fee realized client outcomes; Portfolio turnover, tracking and servicing costs; Estate settlements and retained assets; Recipient client acquisition

Break condition: The premium-service thesis fails if clients move back to pooled products or realized net benefits do not support incremental fees. For an incumbent, the thesis fails if intergenerational attrition exceeds assets won from other providers and settlement fees.

Themes: Tax-aware customization creates a premium service niche Inheritance moves wealth and puts adviser retention at risk Parental gifts change who can enter ownership

14. Private-label manufacturing with margin discipline

Shelf-space shifts can increase units without increasing supplier profit. Contracts, input pass-through and customer concentration decide how much value is retained by manufacturers versus retailers.

Exposures: MCB (LSE); POST (NYSE); WMT (NASDAQ); COST (NASDAQ)

Valuation gate: Use normalized margins after cost recovery and maintenance investment; separate acquisition earnings from organic demand. Pay for durable customer retention and cash earnings, not an undifferentiated discount-retail label.

Monitor: Organic private-label volumes; Contract repricing cadence; Cash conversion and net debt; Unit share by category; Repeat purchase

Break condition: More own-brand shelf space fails to raise utilization or contract economics remain below the cost of capital. Store-brand unit share reverses after controlling for category mix, or retailer margin fails to improve.

Themes: Store-brand factories can grow volumes without gaining margin Retailers capture the shift to store brands

15. Consumer-credit and collection cash economics

Greater need for credit can worsen lender returns. Loss-adjusted cohort cash flows, funding and collections per dollar invested are more informative than origination growth.

Exposures: OMF (NYSE); ECPG (NASDAQ); PRG (NYSE); Consumer ABS: tranche-specific loss waterfall, duration and liquidity; not a generic beneficiary.

Valuation gate: Stress net losses, cost of debt, leverage and capital returns. No price, yield or target is verified; use a full credit cycle rather than one profitable quarter. Discount cash collections after operating cost, taxes and replacement portfolio purchases; accounting revenue and adjusted EBITDA are insufficient proxies for distributable cash.

Monitor: Vintage cumulative net losses; Approval and collateral mix; Loss-adjusted yield; Funding spreads and liquidity runway; Cash collection versus original underwriting by vintage

Break condition: Reject a bullish volume thesis if mature-vintage contribution or capital returns deteriorate after controlling for growth-related provision accounting. Reject if new-vintage realized returns fall below funding and servicing costs despite apparently cheap portfolio prices.

Themes: Nonprime credit demand can grow while lender returns fall Default creates portfolio supply, not guaranteed recoveries Lease-to-own solves an upfront gap but may raise lifetime cost

16. Scarcity-led personalization and collection stewardship

Wealth can support value per scarce item and recurring care for the installed stock. This is a conditional research avenue: expectations, illiquidity and utilization can consume the apparent premium.

Exposures: RACE (NYSE); CB (NYSE); Private specialist workshops, secure vehicle storage and collection-management businesses; verify customer concentration, insurance and technician retention.; Specialized art-storage facilities and operating businesses: Potential recurring fees tied to the collection stock. Risk: Facility utilization, catastrophe exposure and specialist labor.

Valuation gate: No live valuation or mispricing conclusion established for RACE. Reverse-underwrite the current multiple against sustainable revenue per car, cash conversion and a less favorable product mix. Avoid capitalizing today's margin or backlog as a perpetual guarantee. Value recurring custody/service contribution separately from transport and transactions. No storage-parent ticker is assigned without verifying segment materiality; CB requires whole-company underwriting diligence.

Monitor: Personalization contribution and mix versus shipments and price.; Order cancellations, deposit conversion and used-car price retention.; Industrial free cash flow after product investment.; Workshop hours, technician retention and revenue per occupied storage space.; Storage occupancy and contract renewal

Break condition: If personalization slows, allocations cease to be scarce, residual values weaken enough to reduce customer demand, or recurring service costs absorb revenue, the scarcity-based profit thesis weakens. Reject the resilience thesis if storage and stewardship revenue falls in lockstep with auction turnover or retention requires uneconomic discounts.

Themes: Scarce cars monetize personalization more than unit volume The stock of collections supports stewardship between sales

A reading guide

Mechanism first. Security second.

Every theme begins with a household or balance-sheet change. The short explanation identifies the economic response. Industry beneficiaries and losers come next; tickers are specific exposures, often imperfect ones.

Evidence has three levels

Observed: a documented relationship or operating result, which may still be descriptive. Plausible: a supported mechanism whose attribution or size is not established. Hypothesis: a testable possibility with weak or incomplete evidence. High / medium / low confidence refers to the stated mechanism, not a probability of stock-price gains.

Orders describe the path, not the company forever

A business can be directly affected in one theme and a supplier in another. Cards are grouped by ticker and transmission order. When its theme contexts disagree, the card is yellow and each underlying effect remains visible. Filters apply to the shown contexts, not a universal company rating.

What makes an industry a beneficiary or loser?

A beneficiary has a plausible route to demand, pricing, utilization or cost advantages. A loser faces displaced spending, lower activity, compressed margins or funding constraints. These effects may reverse in a severe recession or when supply responds. Unmet need is not automatically payable demand.

Horizon and valuation

Near = 0–2 years; medium = 2–5; long = 5–10. Structural tailwinds do not establish cheapness. Selected dated valuation work from the original research remains available in the package; it is not a live quote service or a buy/sell rating.

Coverage and boundaries

Lower-income and wealthy households are heterogeneous. Income is not wealth; business growth does not prove a demographic motive. Gambling, clinical care, status and dating hypotheses receive explicit causal and funding caveats.
